clue.text: Panic is emanating from fish-pond

indicators.note: emanating suggests letters flowing out and re-forming, so the words panic is are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something in a state of panic is fleeing from a fish-pond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emanating' signals the anagram of PANIC IS; 'from' is a link. A piscina is chiefly a church basin, but its Latin root sense is a fish-pond.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for a fish-pond, also used in English for an ornamental pool where fish are kept.

clue.text: Person drawing rope

explanation.surface: A person drawing a rope, perhaps in a tug of war.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist is someone drawing or making pictures, and on a boat the mooring line at the bow has the same name.

clue.text: Pay enough for supporting life

parts.note: a description of earnings that cover only the bare necessities of staying alive

explanation.definitionFit: Earnings just sufficient to keep a worker fed and housed, with nothing to spare.

clue.text: I get the most out of widescreen cinema

parts.note: max is short for maximum, the most possible

explanation.surface: A film fan claims to enjoy a big screen to the full.
explanation.definitionFit: A trademarked format of very large cinema screens and the theatres built for them.

clue.text: Sake can be poured out obliquely

indicators.note: pouring out a liquid tips it into a new shape, so the words sake can are rearranged

explanation.surface: Japanese rice wine can be served at an angle.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking at something sideways, with suspicion or a slanting glance.

clue.text: At intervals one after another

explanation.surface: Two ways of describing things happening in sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Alternately, each in turn: things done in rotation happen at intervals and in succession.

clue.text: Ceremonial dinner from bar in silence I leave

parts.note: to bar something is to ban it

indicators.note: the letter I is told to leave the word quiet, so it is dropped

parts.note: silence is quiet

explanation.surface: A formal dinner held in a bar, where I leave the quiet behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' takes I out of QUIET to give QUET; 'from' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand formal feast, often with speeches, held on an official occasion.

clue.text: Let oneself go to this community

explanation.surface: Someone abandoning restraint and heading for a community.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'go to town' is an idiom for doing something lavishly, without restraint, so the first part is a fill-in-the-blank definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom go to ___ means behave without restraint, and a settlement larger than a village is a community.

clue.text: Pour water on animals

explanation.surface: Someone pouring water over their pets.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for heavy rain is read literally as rain falling on two kinds of animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to rain very heavily, and taken literally it is rain falling on felines and canines.

clue.text: Where has - - - - ? To illegal liquor shop

definitions.text: Where has - - - - ? To illegal liquor shop

parts.words: Where has - - - - ? To illegal liquor shop
parts.note: a question with blanks: fill them with a pronoun and a past participle to ask where a woman has been, and the reply names an unlicensed bar

explanation.walkthrough: The blanks hide a two-word phrase, a pronoun plus a participle, which run together spell an Irish word for an illicit drinking den.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish and Scottish term for an unlicensed bar selling drink illegally.

clue.text: Not colourful when written down

explanation.surface: A plain monochrome description of something set down on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Monochrome is literally without colour, and the idiom means set down in writing or print.

clue.text: Double to win no less

indicators.note: less means minus, so the O is subtracted from the words to win

parts.note: O is a zero, nought, so it can stand for no

explanation.surface: A gambler doubles their stake in order to win, no less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' is O (nothing), and 'less' takes it out of TO WIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A double is an exact duplicate or lookalike, as one sibling of a pair born together is.

clue.text: A snug resort in Scotland

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort again, so the letters of a snug are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A cosy holiday resort somewhere in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' poses as a holiday place but is re-sort, the anagram signal. The definition is just a place in Scotland: Angus is a council area on the east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish county and council area north of Dundee, so a place found in Scotland.

clue.text: Airman, he has pain

parts.note: AC is aircraftman, the lowest RAF rank
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pilot is said to be suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull continuous pain, the noun used for a sore head or tooth.

clue.text: Feeling of discontent about love for messenger

indicators.note: the feeling is placed around, about, the love letter

parts.note: envy is discontent at another's good fortune
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A resentful envoy grudges someone else's love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts O (love, nil in tennis) inside ENVY.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomatic representative sent to carry messages between governments.

clue.text: Orange current?

parts.note: reads like an electric flow in a colour, but it is what is squeezed from the fruit, and slang also uses the word for electricity

explanation.definitionFit: The liquid pressed from an orange; it is also informal slang for electric power.

clue.text: Entourage mutineer riotously but not to start with

indicators.note: riotous behaviour is wild and disorderly, so the letters are scrambled
the opening letter of mutineer is not to be included

explanation.surface: A celebrity's hangers-on behave like a riotous mutineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not to start with' drops the M of MUTINEER; 'riotously' rearranges UTINEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the group of attendants who accompany an important person.

clue.text: Ripped, say, to the north of 6

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, so its sound matters, not its spelling

parts.note: ripped means torn
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Something torn apart lies to the north of a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is 6-down, TOWN. In non-rhotic British speech TORN sounds like TAUN; 'of' is a link. TAUNTON is the county town of Somerset.
explanation.definitionFit: Taunton is the county town of Somerset in south-west England, a town by example.

clue.text: Discover something missing?

parts.note: a find is something discovered
out means absent or missing

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to discover what has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading: a find (something) that is out (missing).
explanation.definitionFit: To learn or uncover a fact by enquiry, the phrasal verb for coming to know.

clue.text: Giving support to minor footballer

parts.note: to be for something is to support it
a ward is a minor under a guardian's protection

explanation.surface: A coach backing a young player.
explanation.definitionFit: A forward is an attacking player in football, playing nearest the opposing goal.

clue.text: Brownie food?

parts.note: suggests a snack for a young Girl Guide or a chocolate cake, but means food that has been browned under a grill

explanation.definitionFit: A grilled sandwich, browned by heat, hence playful brownie food.

clue.text: Penny not right among fruit-trees to have duck

indicators.note: not means the R is left out of the trees

parts.note: an orchard is a plantation of fruit trees

explanation.surface: A penny-pinching orchard owner keeps a duck among the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes one R from ORCHARD to leave OCHARD; 'among' and 'to have' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A pochard is a diving bird, a type of wildfowl common in Europe.

clue.text: Not hit below the belt during fight

explanation.surface: A boxer avoids a low blow in a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part reads the phrase literally: a blow aimed high rather than low.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a blow aimed high, never low, and as an idiom a brawl or scuffle.

clue.text: Decarbonised fuel requiring no energy in the act

indicators.note: the shortened fuel sits in the middle of the act

parts.note: a deed is an act

indicators.note: the fuel goes without, needs no, energy, so that letter is removed

parts.note: coke is a solid fuel made from coal
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Fuel that needs no energy has been decarbonised in the process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requiring no' and 'in' are the deletion and container signals; 'the act' looks like a theatrical scene but is just a deed. Decoking was routine car-engine maintenance.
explanation.definitionFit: To decoke an engine is to remove carbon deposits from it, so a cleaned engine is decarbonised.

clue.text: River fish, it is attached to fishing-rod

parts.note: an eel is a snake-like fish

explanation.surface: An angler catches a river fish on a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is the winding device fixed to a rod for paying out and retrieving line.

clue.text: May French going to new Zealand port

parts.note: mai is the French word for the month of May

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman named May sails to a New Zealand harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new Zealand' is read as NZ; 'going to' is a link. Mainz is a German city with a river port on the Rhine.
explanation.definitionFit: Mainz is a German city on the Rhine with a major inland harbour.

clue.text: Old pupil left 99 of the poems

indicators.note: the pupil has left, gone from the word old

parts.note: L for learner, a pupil driver
IC is 99 in Roman numerals: one before a hundred

explanation.surface: An old pupil left behind ninety-nine poems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' means L, the pupil, departs from OLD, leaving OD. IC as 99 is a loose crossword Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Odic is the adjective for odes, so relating to those lyric verses.

clue.text: Cut cakes up

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: buns are small sweet cakes

explanation.surface: Someone slices cakes into pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone is to snub or ignore them deliberately.

clue.text: Spots teenagers sometimes have to face

definitions.text: Spots teenagers sometimes have to face

parts.words: Spots teenagers sometimes have to face
parts.note: face reads as confront, but these are pimples literally on the face of young people

explanation.definitionFit: A skin condition producing pimples, common in adolescence.

clue.text: Making an effort to achieve shortest time while going backwards

definitions.text: Making an effort to achieve shortest time

explanation.surface: A runner racing for a record while heading in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is literal: moving counter to the direction of a clock's hands.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means racing to finish within a deadline, and literally it means turning anticlockwise.

clue.text: You once got in new blade that was liable to change colour

indicators.note: the old pronoun gets inside the rearranged blade
new signals that the letters of blade are given a fresh order

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: In days gone by, you were handed a new blade that tended to discolour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal and 'got in' the container; 'You once' points to archaic English. 'that was' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dyeable can take a tint, so it can be given a different hue.

clue.text: Did some ironing when in a hurry

explanation.surface: Someone ironing clothes when short of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing clothes smooths them with an iron, and someone pressed for time is rushed.
